lessons.title: Positioning the test kit and reference card
steps: Lay the used test kit flat on a plain, non-reflective surface.
Place the reference card in the SAME plane as the reaction area, directly beside it.
Both must be in one frame: the card is the measurement reference for that specific exposure.
Do not photograph the card separately and the sample separately. The transform is only valid for the frame it was estimated from.

lessons.title: Lighting
steps: Use even, diffuse light. Open shade outdoors is better than direct sun.
Avoid a single bare bulb or a phone torch at close range; both create a specular highlight the glare gate will reject.
Avoid mixed lighting, for example daylight through a window plus a fluorescent tube, where different parts of the frame sit under different illuminants.
Do not let your own shadow, or the phone's, fall across the card or the sample.

lessons.title: Distance and angle
steps: Hold the phone roughly 20-30 cm from the surface.
Keep the sensor plane parallel to the surface. A tilted shot makes the card patches trapezoidal and the sampled areas wrong.
Move closer if the app says the card occupies too little of the frame: small patches are averaged over too few pixels to be a useful reference.

lessons.title: Avoiding blur
steps: Brace your elbows or rest the phone against a stable object.
Let autofocus settle before capturing.
Use CHECK FRAME: it reports the measured sharpness against the kit profile's threshold rather than leaving you to judge by eye.

lessons.title: Reading the result
steps: PRESUMPTIVE POSITIVE means the calibrated colour fell inside the kit profile's positive region and every quality check passed.
PRESUMPTIVE NEGATIVE means the same for the negative region.
INCONCLUSIVE means the system declined to report an outcome. It is a valid, useful result, not a failure.
Every result requires confirmatory laboratory testing regardless of which of the three it is.

lessons.title: Understanding reliability status
steps: PASS: all measured values were within the kit profile's limits.
REVIEW REQUIRED: something needs a human to look at it - a borderline colour, a quality value outside limits, or a disagreement between the model and the profile rules.
RECAPTURE REQUIRED: a blocking problem such as a missing card or failed calibration. No colour measurement was reported.
The status is a three-state indicator, not a percentage. No validation data exists that would justify a numeric reliability score.

lessons.title: What anomalies mean
steps: Each anomaly is a named code attached to a measurement and the threshold it crossed.
An anomaly describes what was observed. It never asserts a cause and never asserts intent.
ANOMALY_LOCATION_INTEGRITY in particular means only that distance and elapsed time between two records imply an unusual speed. Poor GPS, a clock change and legitimate fast travel all produce it.

lessons.title: The evidence record
steps: Every completed test produces a record containing identity, context, result, versions and integrity values.
The original image is hashed with SHA-256 the moment it is written, and is never modified.
Each record commits to the previous record's hash, so altering any historical record breaks the chain from that point on.
The record is signed with an Ed25519 key generated on this device and held in platform secure storage.
Signing shows a record has not changed since creation. It does not prove the real-world time of capture, and it does not prove which institution the key belongs to.

lessons.title: Safety
steps: Follow the kit manufacturer's handling, PPE and disposal instructions in full.
Keep the reference card clear of reagents and samples.
Retain the physical sample and follow your organisation's procedure for laboratory submission.
